questions.q:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The sky appeared to be greyest after the storm.
questions.s:
The underlined word greyest is a superlative adjective, implying comparison among three or more items, which is not supported by the sentence context (no multiple items are compared). The sentence requires a simple adjective to describe the sky's appearance.

more grey: Comparative, implying comparison with another, not suitable without a specific comparison.

greyer: Comparative, also incorrect without a comparison.

most grey: Superlative, similar to "greyest," incorrect without multiple items.

grey: Base adjective, appropriate for a simple description: "The sky appeared to be grey after the storm."

Thus, grey is the correct alternative.

o: The condition of his health
is getting more and more worse

questions.s: Only "worse and worse" or "more and more bad", not both together.

questions.q: He runs (a) / very fastly (b) / in races. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Fastly' is incorrect; the correct adverb is 'fast.' Answer: (b). 'Fastly' galat hai, sahi adverb hai 'fast.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: The wedding gown / looked decently / despite being / studded with jewels.
o: The wedding gown
despite being
looked decently
studded with jewels
questions.s:
Explanation:- (c) Use 'decent' instead of 'decently' kyunki looked yahan linking verb hai aur linking verb ke baad adjective ka use hota hai 'decently' adverb aur 'decent' adjective hai.

Note:- look verb ka matlab jab 'dekhna' hota hai tab yeh verb action verb hoti hai. Jab look verb ka matlab 'dikhayi padna' hota hai tab yeh linking verb hoti hai.

Eg:- (a) She is looking at me (action verb)

       (b) She looks sad (linking verb)

questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

In the kitchen, the knife, with its sleek design and fantastic engineering, was a sharpest, effortlessly slicing through the ripe tomatoes to demonstrate its superior cutting ability.
o: In the kitchen, the knife, with its sleek design and fantastic engineering
through the ripe tomatoes to demonstrate its superior cutting ability
was a sharpest, effortlessly slicing
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'was a sharpest, effortlessly slicing '.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'was the sharpest, effortlessly slicing' should be used instead of 'was a sharpest, effortlessly slicing'.
  • The given sentence is an example of a Superlative Degree.
  • We know that the definite article 'the' is always used before a superlative degree. Here, in the given question 'sharpest' is a superlative degree of 'sharp'.
  • Superlative Degree: This degree denotes the highest quality and is used when one thing/person is compared to all other things/ persons. 
    • Example: Mohan is the smartest boy in the class. 
  • The use of "the sharpest" is correct in this context because it specifies a particular knife in the kitchen, the one that is the sharpest among all the knives available. By using "the," it indicates that there is a specific knife being referred to, and it is the sharpest one. 
     

Correct Sentence: In the kitchen, the knife, with its sleek design and fantastic engineering, was the sharpest, effortlessly slicing through the ripe tomatoes to demonstrate its superior cutting ability.

questions.q: She is (a) / more happy (b) / than her sister. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Happier' is the comparative form; 'more happy' is incorrect. Answer: (b). 'More happy' galat hai, sahi comparative form hai 'happier.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q:
Select the appropriate option for the given blank-

________ money I had saved up was not enough to buy the car I wanted.
questions.s:
Few and many are used with plural countable nouns. Little and much are used with singular non-count nouns. Little and few have negative meanings. We use them to mean 'not as much as may be expected or wished for'

A few mistakes were found in the paper. → some, a small number

Few errors were there in the paper. → not many/almost none

The few remarks that he made were very suggestive. → The few = not many, but all there are

Jenna has a little money. → some, a small amount

Jenna has little money to spend. → not much/almost nothing

The little information he had was not quite reliable. → The little = not much, but all there is.

Here, the use of 'the little' will be correct to describe that all the money that person has is not enough to buy a car.

The correct sentence is - The little money I had saved up was not enough to buy the car I wanted.

Hence, option (d) is correct.
